label: AUDIT of a dry run. Decomposes the sh_admit backlog charge into its queue part, -mu * max(busy - H, 0), and its A6 part, -mu * a6_backlog, per branch and as a delta.

answer.question: what dominates the backlog charge on sh_admit, and does a6_backlog cancel
answer.answer: the QUEUE part is the entire charge; a6_backlog contributes nothing and is itself exactly ZERO in BOTH branches of every sh_admit candidate at every size, which is stronger than cancelling
answer.why: _prefix_risk produces restore work only for at-risk RC jobs, and an SH admission neither creates nor endangers one
answer.consequence: the escalated a6_backlog units defect cannot explain F-A8 and would NOT help the dashcam axis; it is worth attention for RECALL only

f_a8_mechanism.reading: the fraction carrying a non-zero queue charge tracks the fraction refused to within 0.004 at every size, so a non-zero queue backlog charge is very nearly necessary and sufficient for refusal; and mu itself rises from 1.44 to 9.84 with load while the per-instant gain stays at p50 0.055, which is the amplifier

g1e.verdict: PASS, byte-identical as pre-registered, verified independently of session 1

f5b_sv_synthesis.session1: the state-value SUM PER BRANCH is median 0.009216 with B1+F3 and exactly zero in 100 percent once F2 is added
f5b_sv_synthesis.mine: sv_delta, the DIFFERENCE between branches, is exactly zero in 124,354 of 124,354 candidates, with F2 on AND with every switch off
f5b_sv_synthesis.synthesis: both are right and they are different quantities; with F2 OFF the value is non-zero per branch and STILL CANCELS in DeltaJ, so making it non-zero per branch would not by itself let it influence any decision
f5b_sv_synthesis.p9_update: P9 must test BOTH non-zero per branch AND a non-zero difference between branches, and the second is what decides whether the channel can affect anything
